subject: Re: Evidence request — training/retention opt-out, DPIA, and HIPAA considerations
messages:
From: Julie Wong <julie.wong@acmehealth.com>
To: priya_natarajan@redwood.com
Cc: compliance@acmehealth.com
Date: Tue, 2 Dec 2025 09:15:00 -0800
Subject: LLM training / retention questions + DPIA evidence request

Hi Priya,

Thanks for taking this — Acme Security & Privacy needs to confirm a few items before we can proceed with a production pilot. Please can you provide written confirmation and any supporting evidence for the items below? We need enough detail to include in our DPIA and to present to internal risk committees.

Key questions:
- Do you ever use customer prompts, responses, or metadata to train or fine-tune models (including internal research/ops experiments)? If yes, please describe conditions and opt-out mechanism.
- What is your default prompt/response retention period on the hosted API? Are there controls to disable or shorten retention for specific customers?
- Can you provide an electronical flow showing how data moves through Redwood (ingest -> KV cache -> storage -> telemetry)? We need to show where PHI would be visible.
- Do you offer a contractual BAA for customers with PHI? If so, which deployment options (hosted/dedicated/private) are covered?
- Are SCCs or equivalent transfer mechanisms available for international data flows?
- Please attach SOC 2 Type II summary, a DPIA statement, and any redaction/opt-out playbook.

Timeline: we are aiming to close this review by Dec 11. If you can acknowledge receipt and estimated delivery time for the evidence pack that would be great.

Thanks,
Julie
Julie Wong
Head of Security and Privacy, Acme Health
compliance@acmehealth.com

From: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.com>
To: Julie Wong <julie.wong@acmehealth.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, rishi_malhotra@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 2 Dec 2025 11:02:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: LLM training / retention questions + DPIA evidence request

Hi Julie — thanks for the clear list. Acknowledged.

Short answers up front while we assemble the pack:
- Training on customer data: by default Redwood does NOT use customer prompts or responses to continually train or fine-tune public models. Customers who opt in to collaborative research or data-sharing programs are explicitly consented.
- Retention: hosted API default retention window for request/response artifacts is 30 days for debugging and reliability metrics; we offer a configurable retention policy and an option to disable request-level retention for customers on Dedicated or Private deployments.
- BAA / HIPAA: we can sign a BAA; BAAs are supported for Dedicated and Private deployments. For Hosted API we evaluate on a case-by-case basis (need details on PHI types and risk controls).
- SCCs / transfers: SCCs and other EU transfer mechanisms are available as addenda for contracts.

I'll coordinate an evidence package (SOC 2 summary, DPIA statement, architecture/data flow diagram, and our training opt-out playbook). Target delivery: EOD Thu, Dec 4.

Two quick clarifying questions for your DPIA team:
1) Do you expect Redwood to attest that no customer data has ever been used in model training historically, or is a forward-looking opt-out attestation sufficient?
2) Will you need redaction/PII-scanning logs for verification, or are high-level controls (encryption, access logs, retention policies) acceptable?

Looping in Marissa from Customer Solutions for deployment options, and Rishi from Legal for contract addenda.

Best,
Priya Natarajan
Head of Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
Phone: +1 (415) 555-0138

From: Julie Wong <julie.wong@acmehealth.com>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.com>
Cc: compliance@acmehealth.com, luis.fernandez@acmehealth.com
Date: Wed, 3 Dec 2025 08:47:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: LLM training / retention questions + DPIA evidence request

Thanks Priya — helpful. A couple quick answers:
- For our DPIA we need a forward-looking attestation that Acme data will not be used for model training without explicit written consent plus a statement on historical use. If you can say historical use is none, that is preferred; if not, please disclose the scope.
- We will need the data flow diagram showing where PHI may be present and any safeguards around KV cache and logs.
- For HIPAA/BAA: Acme requires a BAA for any environment that processes PHI. We expect BAAs for Dedicated or Private; need to know if Hosted can be included under any circumstance.

We appreciate the EOD Thu target for materials. Please include the contact who will sign the BAA and the typical turnaround for legal review.

Julie

From: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.com>
To: Julie Wong <julie.wong@acmehealth.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, rishi_malhotra@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 4 Dec 2025 13:10:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Evidence package — attached: SOC2 summary, DPIA statement, dataflow

Hi Julie — attached is the evidence pack as requested. Files included: redwood-soc2-summary.pdf, redwood-dpia-statement.docx, data-flow-diagram.png. I have also included a short guidance note below about training and opt-out controls.

Summary guidance (high level):
- Historical training: Redwood confirms that we have not used customer prompts/responses from the hosted API for model training or fine-tuning of our public model catalog without explicit, documented customer consent. We can provide a statement for your DPIA.
- Opt-out & exclusions: Customers may request a training-exclusion flag at the tenant/account level. For Hosted API this flag prevents any of the account's request/response data from being included in internal research pools or annotations. For Dedicated and Private deployments the default is isolation (no training), and retention controls are under customer control.
- Retention & deletion: Default hosted retention is 30 days; data owners may request deletion earlier via support ticket. For Dedicated/Private deployments, retention is configurable and deletions can be handled via API and audit logs.
- PHI / BAA: Redwood can execute a BAA for Dedicated and Private deployments. Hosted deployments may be considered for BAAs for select enterprise customers after an architecture review and additional controls.
- SCCs & transfers: SCCs and EU transfer addenda are available as contract attachments.

Next steps:
1) I will share the formal attestation language for inclusion in your DPIA by end of day tomorrow.
2) If you would like, Marissa can schedule a short architecture walk-through (30 min) to review the data flow and caching behavior.
3) Rishi is available to review BAA terms and SCC addenda.

Attachments:
- redwood-soc2-summary.pdf (SOC 2 Type II summary; redacted)
- redwood-dpia-statement.docx (DPIA/attestation draft)
- data-flow-diagram.png (high-level flow showing ingress, KV cache, telemetry, long-term storage boundaries)

Best,
Priya
Priya Natarajan
Head of Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Julie Wong <julie.wong@acmehealth.com>, priya_natarajan@redwood.com
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 4 Dec 2025 14:22:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Evidence package — legal clarifications on BAA/SCCs

Hi Julie — quick legal note:
- BAA: Redwood Legal can execute a BAA for Dedicated and Private deployments; for Hosted deployments we are open to consideration but would require an architecture review and specific ingress controls documented in the contract.
- SCCs: We provide SCC addenda for EU transfers.
- Attestation language: We can provide the forward-looking attestation Priya referenced and a historical statement: currently Redwood does NOT use customer prompts/responses from the hosted API for model training without explicit consent. We will provide the signed attestation as a PDF for your records.

If you confirm the scope (which Acme accounts/environments are in-scope) we can prepare the BAA and SCC addenda drafts and target a 5-business-day turnaround for initial review.

Regards,
Rishi Malhotra
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
